title: Tried adding some crackle and vfx to my sword trails, is it too much??
author: Cosmonan
selftext: Hello, guys! I used Claude Code with Unity MCP to create a Kirby Crackle trail effect and add some elemental VFX to the trail, but I am not sure if it is too much going on. How do you guys think it can be improved?

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: what if the trails were themselves holy swords?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: What do you mean by holy swords?

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: He particle effects already kind of looked like swords.  Made me think what if they look like kind of glowing blue swords, pointing downwards like a cross.

comments.author: HLCYSWAP
comments.body:
reminds me of everything i hate about jrpgs. needless flourishing of eyesore vfx

I feel like vfx and animations should be doing a handshake: what is the animation NOT doing that the vfx MUST do instead? convey power of strike. so, personally, I would instead make the flame go alpha <much> faster and have a ground slam effect, while unifying all effects to be one color and one shape

currently its an eyesore for me and thats just 1 guy doing 1 move with 1 weapon. imagine putting 5 enemies on screen, with 2-3 vfx each that have these sort of overengineering. it would get tiresome fast, for me

there is a market for this kind of style. its not me

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: Thanks for the comment! Indeed, I think its too much right now... Do you mean leaving the trail with a single color (like white) for every attack and just leave the electrical / flame effect? Also agree on making the flames disappear faster.

replies.author: HLCYSWAP
replies.body:
you could do white, thats a style i think botw did. its up to you. if you keep the flame i would tone it down a lot and get the shape of the flame more focused and nearly mono-color within itself. (white, red, orange, not two shades of red with different shaders)

the eyes of your users are a finite space. think about what you want to be meaningful on screen. is it sparse, like botw, where heavy flourishes are ok? is it packed, like musou games where you literally cannot afford to waste screen space? 

that's where you come in and decide what is important to you

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: Thank you for the tips, man! Yeah, I didnt record the video in a combat scene, but it is definitely too much, even more if I consider there is perfect dodge with visual prompt, so this would certainly affect visibility. Will tone down a bit and make some changes to the flames.

comments.author: tastygnar
comments.body: Its a lot and its awesome but id want to see more to know if it's too much, just right, or not enough

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: Thank you! I will come back after some adjustments. Right now it is definitely too much.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Something that has worked for me is to ask the AI to do a sort of "flourish pass" on whatever we are doing. It has diminishing returns on something but at least once usually leads to a better result.

comments.author: idkwtftbhmeh
comments.body: looks nice just explain to the model that it looks like it's repeating forms of the pattern all over the flow of the particle, try to make it look like a one single flow

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: Yeah, that would be ideal, but I didnt manage to make it work yet... I thinks thats because of the VFXs I am using, but I need to check my library, maybe theres something better there.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body:
Needs something louder when the sword slams down, and maybe an effect as well.

Also, this is a long animation that, depending on your game mechanics, has the player vulnerabile for counterattacks for some time. It needs to be worth it, e.g. make the final slam an aoe.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: The slam is definitely lacking now, gonna tackle that, thanks for the tip!

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
This turns your character into a cloud lol. 

I think you should tone it down for now. You can find some reference videos on youtube, where they showcase various VFX in a gray room. Then you can borrow ideas from them. But i think, you'll better to make levels and enemies first, and attack with no VFX, then add VFX later. This helps you to not overdo the VFX. Remember that games shouldn't be pretty, they should be readable

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Thanks for the tips, man!

Yeah, I already have a full gameplay loop, only 3 different enemies, but it is already working.  
I have increased particle spacing and reduced opacity, it got a little better already, gotta fine tune it.

comments.author: TradeNPlayz
comments.body: Doesn't look too bad for early stage. Only thing I'd remove are the black spots.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: I am not too sure about them as well, but I really want to make this kind of crackle work, and would be a cool visual identity if I can make it work, I guess...

comments.author: blessed--
comments.body: damn my unity mcp could never make sword trails like this, even with reference to hundreds of vfx prefabs i own lol. mind educating me on how to do this?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: The color trail shader was made straight from claude to unity mcp, by using some reference images and description prompt. The fire and electrical VFX is a second shader made from VFXs prefabs I already had, also just description prompt and prefab reference.

replies.author: blessed--
replies.body: damn i guess i just couldnt describe it correctly, i gave it some ref images and it was able to nail it. thnx lol

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: The fire particles are too repetitive imo as they appear to be tiling in the air. The others are simple enough to not have that same problem.  Would probably not make them the default, however. Particles like this are only great when highlighting something special, not when it becomes the norm you have to build even further upon to stand out.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: Yep, you are correct. I reduced the particle number for the fire trail and got so much better. Also changed the elemental mechanic to use energy and only triggered when pressing R2 . Thanks for ghe feedback

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Way too much sauce my guy, suggestions: tuning it down by 60-70% and adding a strong dissipating fade to it so where it fades away stronger and creates more of a true trailing effect.
